decision_rule: The first checkpoint whose boundary ratio reaches 0.3 is compared against the formation step. At or before it, the reading is BOUNDARY_WITH_COUNTER: fine-grained precision arrives with usability. Strictly later, the reading is BOUNDARY_AFTER_COUNTER: precision arrives only after the counter is already usable. A ratio that never reaches 0.3 is BOUNDARY_NOT_FORMED_BY_FINAL, which contradicts the gate cell and names an instrument fault. If no formation step exists the comparison has no left-hand side, which is recorded as BOUNDARY_TIMING_UNDEFINED_NO_FORMATION; a passing gate makes that unreachable, and it is named here rather than left to be invented later.
metric: The first checkpoint whose boundary ratio reaches 0.3, compared against the formation step.
notes: The boundary's own first crossing of 0.3 is a separate recorded observable, not the start of its stability window; the committed gate record settles that in its fourth answer of record. Comparing that crossing against the formation step asks whether fine-grained precision arrives with usability or only later. The boundary ratio is the mean of the profile's first two parts minus the mean of its last two. Its bar stays absolute at 0.3, with no baseline correction, because the smaller sibling's untrained checkpoint read -0.080316, which is effectively zero. On that sibling's final checkpoint the ratio reads -0.090673, so the boundary is absent at 410 million weights and present at 1.4 billion. That is why this formation sweep runs on the larger model. If either integrity gate recorded in these values failed, this record is void as evidence about the model, and is an instrument fault only. A further run of this script on the same box is a rerun of the same instrument, not a replication.
